slides.say: a and b are integers. Given: a minus b is equal to six. Which of the following expressions is necessarily even?
So we know the difference, six, and we look for the expression that's always even. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, with the parities, and then plugging in numbers.

[short pause] Let's start with the parities. Six is even, and when is a difference even? When both are even, like eight minus two, or both are odd, like nine minus three. So a and b have the same parity.

Now choice number two, b squared plus a b. Take out b, and it's b times, in brackets, b plus a. And b plus a is even plus even or odd plus odd, so it's always even. A product with an even factor is even, so choice number two is our answer.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now let's try plugging in. Which numbers? If I take two even numbers, every choice comes out even, and they won't help. So two odd numbers with a difference of six, a is seven and b is one.
at: a is seven and b is one

slides.say: Choice number one, forty-nine plus one plus five is fifty-five, odd. Out. Choice number two, one plus seven is eight, even. Choice number three, forty-two minus one is forty-one, odd. Out. Choice number four, two forty-five plus four is two forty-nine, odd. Out.
Three are out, so choice number two. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
